QuestionStmt.S: Which of the following transitions in hydrogen atom emit photons of highest frequency? ($n$ = principal quantum number)

Solution.S:
Energy difference $\Delta E = -13.6 \left( \frac{1}{n_f^2} - \frac{1}{n_i^2} \right)$ eV. Higher $\Delta E$ means higher frequency.

Option A: $1 \to 3$ is absorption (not emission).
Option B: $2 \to 4$ is absorption.
Option C: $5 \to 3$: $\Delta E = -13.6(1/9 - 1/25) = -0.967$ eV.
Option D: $2 \to 1$: $\Delta E = -13.6(1/1 - 1/4) = -10.2$ eV.

Thus $2 \to 1$ has the highest energy and hence highest frequency. Correct option is D.
